Yes! That's a clean approach. Here's how the tiered fallback would work:

---

## Tiered Cell Rendering

```ruby
# In ColumnComponent#render_cell(row, view_context)
def render_cell(row, view_context)
  # Tier 1: Block provided
  if @block
    view_context.capture { @block.call(row) }
  
  # Tier 2: Helper method exists (e.g., `render_site_status_cell`)
  elsif view_context.respond_to?(helper_method_name)
    view_context.send(helper_method_name, row)
  
  # Tier 3: Simple value lookup
  else
    value_for(row)
  end
end

def helper_method_name
  :"render_#{row_class_name}_#{key}_cell"  # e.g., render_site_status_cell
end
```

---

## Usage Examples

```erb
<%= render Dashboard::DataTableComponent.new(rows: @sites) do |table| %>
  <%# Tier 3: Simple value %>
  <% table.with_column(key: :name, label: "Name") %>
  
  <%# Tier 2: Auto-discovers `render_site_status_cell` helper %>
  <% table.with_column(key: :status, label: "Status") %>
  
  <%# Tier 1: Explicit block for one-off rendering %>
  <% table.with_column(key: :custom, label: "Custom") do |row| %>
    <%= row.some_special_logic %>
  <% end %>
<% end %>
```

```ruby
# app/helpers/sites_helper.rb
module SitesHelper
  def render_site_status_cell(site)
    if site.production_theme_version_id.present?
      render Ui::BadgeComponent.new(variant: :success, dot: true) { "Published" }
    else
      render Ui::BadgeComponent.new(variant: :warning, dot: true) { "Draft" }
    end
  end

  def render_site_indexing_cell(site)
    variant = site.allow_indexing? ? :success : :danger
    label = site.allow_indexing? ? "Allowed" : "Blocked"
    render Ui::BadgeComponent.new(variant: variant, dot: true) { label }
  end
end
```

---

## Benefits

| Tier | When to Use |
|------|-------------|
| **Block** | One-off or view-specific rendering |
| **Helper** | Reusable across multiple views (sites index, dashboard, etc.) |
| **Value** | Simple text/date display |

This way the status badge logic lives in `SitesHelper` once, and both the sites index and dashboard automatically use it. Want me to implement this?
